definition: Perceiver is a variant of the Transformer architecture, adapted for processing arbitrary forms of data, such as images, sounds and video, and spatial data.
details: Unlike previous notable Transformer systems such as BERT and GPT-3, which were designed for text processing, the Perceiver is designed as a general architecture that can learn from large amounts of heterogeneous data. It accomplishes this with an asymmetric attention mechanism to distill inputs into a latent bottleneck. Perceiver matches or outperforms specialized models on classification tasks. Perceiver was introduced in June 2021 by DeepMind. It was followed by Perceiver IO in August 2021.

explainer.lead: A Transformer variant designed to process arbitrary data such as images, sounds, video and spatial data, not just text. It matters as a general architecture that learns from large amounts of heterogeneous data.

tiers.eli5: Most text-focused AI models read words; this one is built to look at many kinds of input, from pictures to sounds, all with the same setup.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to classification tasks across modalities, where it matches or outperforms specialized models. Its asymmetric attention distills inputs into a latent bottleneck, which caps compute but can discard fine detail.
tiers.paperLevel: The Perceiver uses asymmetric attention to distill inputs into a latent bottleneck, and was introduced by DeepMind in June 2021, followed by Perceiver IO in August 2021.

explainer.example: A team feeds images and audio into a single Perceiver, which compresses each input into a latent bottleneck via cross-attention and then classifies it, matching a specialized model.
